title: Split pea, marrow and broccoli curry pot

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything here is a whole food or a plain cupboard staple, from split peas and curry powder to vegetable stock, so nothing is a factory-built product.

supermarket.reason: Split peas, marrow, broccoli, tomatoes, lemon and coriander are all everyday Tesco items at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded pan, a sieve and a jug, and every step is simple simmering.

works.reason: 250g split peas to 1.2 litres stock, simmered for about 55 minutes with the marrow added later, should give a thick, well-spiced pot for four, and there is a note to loosen it if needed.

honest_times.reason: Twenty-five minutes hands-on covers chopping, peeling and deseeding the marrow plus softening the onion, and 75 minutes total fits the simmering times given.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient appears in the steps, the names match their ids, and the steps use nothing that is not listed.

seasonal_feel.reason: Mid-August marrow is the bulk of the dish alongside seasonal broccoli and tomatoes, and a mild curry pot suits a late-summer lunch.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, homely British English with plain doneness cues a beginner can follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling pulse-and-vegetable meal with plenty of flavour that a family would happily eat again.
